lines.en: English and German are sisters. They share thousands of words, and they change in the same few ways.
Learn those few changes, and the words unlock themselves. These are your cheat codes.
Some words are exactly the same.
Same spelling, same meaning. Only the sound is German.

els.text: Same spelling, same meaning. Only the sound is German.

lines.en: Notice something? In German, every noun starts with a capital letter.
An English D often turns into a German T.

els.text: An English D often turns into a German T.

lines.en: T becomes Z, or double S.
At the start of a word, T becomes Z. In the middle, it becomes double S.

els.text: At the start of a word, T becomes Z. In the middle, it becomes double S.

lines.en: P becomes P F, or F.
P turns into P F at the start, and into F in the middle.

els.text: P turns into P F at the start, and into F in the middle.

lines.en: German has no T H sound. So it uses D, or T.

els.text: German has no T H sound. So it uses D, or T.

lines.en: Y becomes J, and C becomes K.
In German, J sounds like an English Y.

scenes.header: Cheat code 7 · y » j   c » k

els.text: In German, J sounds like an English Y.

lines.en: And the biggest cheat code of all: the endings.
These five endings alone give you more than a thousand words.

els.text: These five endings alone give you more than a thousand words.

lines.en: But careful. A few words are traps.
It's not a gift. It means poison.
It's not a rat. It means advice.
It's not bald. It means soon.
It's not also. It means so.
Now you try. Use the cheat codes and guess the German word.

lines.de: Mein Bruder trinkt Kaffee im Hotel.

lines.en: My brother drinks coffee in the hotel.
Brother, th becomes d. Drinks, d becomes t. Coffee, c becomes k. And hotel is just hotel.
